readout: qubit mode 9.44 GHz · Q ≈ 3,500 · 99.6 % of its inductive energy in the junction · anharmonicity ≈ 690 MHz
caption: A Palace eigenmode simulation of the first-generation SQUAT (the device of Magoon et al.) on sapphire, with the junction leads exactly as drawn on the mask and the 0.22 µm gap between them bridged by the junction's 10.2 nH inductance (EJ/h ≈ 16 GHz). About 1.4 million tetrahedra, graded smoothly from every metal edge down to 50 nm at the junction. Shown is the mesh on the chip surface and the electric-field energy of the qubit's mode (logarithmic colour): it sits across the gap between the two islands and along their edges, and leaks a little into the feedline. Palace finds the mode at 9.44 GHz, with Q ≈ 3,500 from the feedline, 99.6 % of its inductive energy in the junction and an anharmonicity of about 690 MHz; a coarser mesh gives the same to within 1.4 %. That is in line with these devices' 8.8–9.3 GHz design (the measured ones came out at 7.4–8.5 GHz). The next modes, of the box and the feedline, are above 47 GHz. The tunnel barrier itself is modelled as an inductor across the gap, so these are model values. Hover to read values.
